title: Rollout timeline cookbook and daily runbook — Aug 15, 2027 (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working cookbook for a weekday microlaunch of the routing/telemetry change set scheduled for Aug 15–18, 2027. It focuses on a low-risk, progressive traffic migration with explicit hourly runbook steps, telemetry sampling, and a compact rollback matrix. Draft status: decisions and timing still negotiable; use this as the single source for weekend ops rehearsal and on-call briefing.

Scope / what’s in this ship:
- Model routing fallback: new policy that prefers regional low-latency variants for small requests (<256 tokens).
- Telemetry: new token-level latency tag (route_variant) + sampling bump in canary regions.
- Configs: rollout flag and canary percent control added to traffic-router service.
- No infra changes expected (no nodepool resizing).

Primary goals:
1) Validate routing fallbacks do not regress median latency or token throughput for existing routes.
2) Ensure slow-path fallbacks surface as monitored SLO breaches before impacting global traffic.
3) Keep user-visible error-rate < 0.02% and tail latency p95 within +15% of baseline.

Preflight checklist (to be completed 48–2 hours before go):
- [ ] Merge PR: platform#4217 (linked). Owner: Ethan.
- [ ] Rollout flag created in feature-store and tested locally. Owner: Priya.
- [ ] Canary manifest prepared for eu-west-1 and us-west-2. Owner: Luis.
- [ ] Telemetry alert thresholds calculated from baseline window (last 7 days). Owner: Maya.
- [ ] Run smoke tests against staging with feature flag on (synthetic load at 10 rps). Owner: SRE on-duty.
- [ ] Prepare rollback jumpbox and priveleged IAM token. Owner: Infra eng.
- [ ] Draft customer comms & internal status message template. Owner: PM (TBD).

Runbook — Day 0 (Aug 15) — Canary warmup window (08:00–12:00 PDT)
08:00 — Operator sync & quick brief (15m)- Confirm on-call roster, Slack channel #deploy-rollout, Zoom link.- Confirm linked artifacts and owners listed above.
08:15 — Activate feature flag in staging and run canonical smoke suite (10–15m)- If any test failures: abort and capture logs, assign SRE.
09:00 — Canary deploy to eu-west-1 (5% traffic segment)- Start with routing flag set to 5% for a single route group.- Increase telemetry sampling for canary to 100% for route_variant tag.
09:15 — Monitor first 15 minutes: check list- p50/p95/p99 latency per route_variant (dashboard: rollout/latency).- error-rate and 5xx spikes (alert: rollout/5xx-rebound).- token throughput and qps metrics (traffic/throughput).
09:30 — Canary acceptance decision (15m)- If stable: proceed to 20% after 10:00.- If anomalies: roll back to 0% immediately, capture logs, and run postmortem stub.
10:00 — Escalation point: increase to 20% in eu-west-1 and canary in us-west-2 at 5%
11:00 — Noon check-in and telemetry sanity pass- Validate fallback hit-rate; expected fallback ratio < 2% at 20% traffic.
12:00 — Pause for team lunch & extended monitoring (12:00–13:30)

Runbook — Day 1 (Aug 16) — Ramp (09:00–17:00 PDT)
09:00 — Ramp to 50% in canary regions (eu-west-1 / us-west-2)- Validate customer-facing latency SLA windows.
11:00 — If metrics stable, open canary gate for a staged global ramp (see calendar).
14:00 — Ops rehearsal: simulate a node failure and confirm fallback still serves traffic correctly.
16:00 — Pre-merge signoff meeting with product & SRE (15m)
Runbook — Day 2 (Aug 17) — Global rollout window (08:00–16:00 PDT)
08:00 — Begin progressive regional increases per calendar:
- 08:00–09:30: APAC regions (ap-southeast-1, ap-northeast-1) — 10% then 30%
- 10:00–12:00: EU regions (eu-west-1, eu-central-1) — 50% then 80%
- 13:00–15:00: US regions (us-west-2, us-east-1) — 50% then 100%
15:00 — Global 100% target check; hold if any thresholds tripped.

Telemetry sampling & alerting plan:
- Sampling: canary regions at 100% for route_variant; others remain at 5% unless ramping.
- Dashboards: rollout/latency, rollout/fallback-rate, rollout/error-rate, rollout-cost-per-token.
- Key alerts (Pager):
  - rollout/5xx-rebound (>0.02% absolute increase over baseline) — P0
  - rollout/p99-latency-breach (> +40% over baseline) — P0
  - rollout/fallback-rate (>5% sustained 10m) — P1
  - rollout/throughput-drop (>15% drop vs expected) — P1
- Slack: automated perf-summaries posted to #deploy-rollout every 10m during ramp windows.

Rollback matrix (fast decisions):
- If 5xx or p99 latency P0 triggers: immediate rollback to previous routing config (target 0% within 5m). Owner: on-call SRE.
- If fallback-rate P1 triggers and sustained beyond 30m: pause ramp and investigate; rollback if root cause unclear after 60m. Owner: release lead.
- If cost-per-token increases >2x for >60m in production: pause rollout and throttle to canary. Owner: cost engineering.

Communications plan:
- Internal: status updates every 30m posted to #deploy-rollout; full timeline and incident channel if rollback occurs.
- Customer-facing comms: only if user-visible errors exceed 0.02% or we roll back for >2 hours. Draft template in linked_artifacts.

Draft release notes (internal copy):
- Summary: Introduced a routing fallback that biases low-latency regional variants for shorter requests, plus telemetry tagging to help analyze per-variant performance.
- Why: Reduce median end-to-end latency for interactive flows and improve regional resiliency.
- Risk/impact: Small risk of increased tail latency during kernel cold paths; may increase cross-region cost marginally.
- Migration: No client changes required. Ops knob: feature flag named routing-pref-short-variants.
- Rollback plan: feature flag can be toggled to off; immediate rollback instructions documented above.

Open questions & known unknowns:
- How will third-party CDN re-ordering affect p99 in APAC? (Action: run targeted synthetic tests).
- Are existing autoscaling policies adequate if performance changes increase concurrent KV cache size? (Action: SRE to validate).
- Cost accounting: will we see notable egress differences across regions? (Action: finance to sample).

Post-release verification checklist (within 48h):
- [ ] Confirm no customer-facing regressions in top 10 routes.
- [ ] Validate sampling traces for top 3 latencies per region.
- [ ] Run scheduled canary smoke at 2am local on Aug 19 to verify overnight stability.
- [ ] Close rollup notes and link to confluence page for the postmortem draft.

Appendix: quick commands & links (for on-call)
- Toggle flag (ops UI): /feature/routing-pref-short-variants
- Rollback script: ops/rollback/routing_pref_short.sh (runbook-runner)
- Dashboards: https://grafana.redwood/board/rollout-overview
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4217
- Jira epic: ENG-4312

Notes to self (scratch):
- keep the ramp tempo conservative if APAC synthetic shows >10% p99 change.
- prepare a 1-page FAQ for support teams describing fallback behavior.
- schedule a 1-hour retro 72h after global 100% completes.

Owners & immediate contacts:
- Release lead: Maya Thompson (pager:Maya_T)
- SRE on-duty: Ethan Zhao (pager:Ethan_Z)
- Platform eng: Priya Nair (Slack:@priya)
